pages.title: Client wire protocol: messages, op codes, encodings, feature bits, forwarding

features.name: MDS client transport (messenger v1/v2, protocol 32, stateful_server policy)
features.description: Clients connect to the rank's MDSMap address vector over msgr v1 (protocol CEPH_MDSC_PROTOCOL=32) or msgr v2 (crc/secure). Client connections use Policy::stateful_server(0): lossless, server never reconnects, reset detection, no required connection features.
features.notes: Kernel v1 sends 32 (linux/net/ceph/messenger_v1.c:386). msgr v2 does not check the protocol number.

features.name: cephx authentication and MDS cap parsing at connect
features.description: Clients authenticate with a cephx authorizer for service 'mds'; MDSDaemon::ms_handle_fast_authentication parses the mds caps string (without mds_lock) and fails authentication if unparsable; ms_handle_accept re-parses into Session::auth_caps.
features.notes: auth_service_required default cephx; cephx_sign_messages default true.

features.name: Connection-to-Session binding and pre-open send queue
features.description: Each client entity (client.<global_id>) has one Session per rank bound to the Connection priv; messages to a session without connection are queued in preopen_out_queue and flushed on accept; MDSRank::get_session can swap an imported open session in for CLIENT_SESSION messages.

features.name: MDS entity naming (mds.<rank>)
features.description: Messenger name is mds.-1 without rank, mds.<gid> in standby-replay, mds.<rank> otherwise; libcephfs derives the sender rank from the message source number.
features.notes: Kernel keys on the connection instead.

features.name: Session open with metadata, CephFS feature bits and metric spec exchange
features.description: REQUEST_OPEN (MClientSession v7) carries metadata map, client feature_bitset_t, metric_spec, flags, cap_auths, oldest_client_tid; after journaling ESession the MDS replies OPEN with CEPHFS_FEATURES_MDS_SUPPORTED (bits 0..24), CEPHFS_METRIC_FEATURES_ALL (bits 0..16) and cap_auths, only if the client has the MIMIC bit.
features.notes: Kernel reads only the first 64 bits of the MDS feature bitmap. The duplicate-OPEN reply (NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE) carries supported_features but no metric_spec; both clients overwrite their copy on every OPEN, so libcephfs loses the metric spec.

features.name: required_client_features enforcement
features.description: Per-fs required bitmap in the MDSMap; REQUEST_OPEN and reconnect are refused with error_string 'missing required features' and existing sessions missing a newly required bit are evicted.

features.name: Feature inference for clients that send no feature bits
features.description: If the client feature set is empty the MDS infers jewel/kraken/luminous bits from ceph_version or kernel_version metadata and connection features.
features.notes: Only relevant for very old clients.

features.name: Session REJECT and blocklist signalling
features.description: REJECT for sessionless, fs not permitted, refuse_client_session (always with error_string), and via send_reject_message for blocklisted (flag SESSION_BLOCKLISTED + 'blocklisted (blacklisted)'), missing features, bad root, duplicate uuid (error_string only for MIMIC clients; without metadata or features the message is v1 and also loses the flag).
features.notes: Kernel detects blocklisting by flag (v5+) or by 'blacklisted' substring.

features.name: Session control ops (renewcaps, stale, recall, flushmsg, force_ro, close, flush_mdlog)
features.description: Wire ops 0..12 of CEPH_SESSION_*; RENEWCAPS echoes seq and trims completed requests by oldest_client_tid; REQUEST_CLOSE requires seq == push_seq; FLUSHMSG/FLUSHMSG_ACK synchronize message streams; REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG flushes the journal.
features.notes: Semantics owned by sessions.md.

features.name: Unknown session op handling (REJECT + evict + blocklist)
features.description: Any unrecognised client session op gets REJECT and the client is evicted with blocklisting.

features.name: MClientRequest versioned head (legacy, v1, v2, v3 with struct_len skip)
features.description: Message v<4 carries the 88-byte legacy head; v>=4 carries ceph_mds_request_head with u16 version: v1 (98 bytes), v2 adds 32-bit ext_num_retry/ext_num_fwd, v3 adds struct_len and owner_uid/owner_gid; decoder skips unknown trailing head bytes per struct_len.
features.notes: Clients pick the head version from MDS bits 18 and 20 and connection FS_BTIME.

features.name: Request flags REPLAY / WANT_DENTRY / ASYNC
features.description: REPLAY: resend after unsafe reply (no early reply, no releases, completed-request lookup, queued for clientreplay in reconnect). WANT_DENTRY: include dentry trace, null dentry on ENOENT. ASYNC: async create/unlink, queued for clientreplay in reconnect.

features.name: Piggy-backed cap and dentry-lease releases in requests
features.description: num_releases records (ceph_mds_request_release + dname) processed before dispatch for non-replay client requests.
features.notes: Dropped for requests resent during up:reconnect with a retry count.

features.name: Request tail fields: stamp, gid_list, alternate_name, fscrypt_auth/file
features.description: Message v2+ stamp (client op time used for ctime/mtime), v4 supplementary gids, v5 alternate_name (fscrypt), v6 fscrypt_auth/fscrypt_file.
features.notes: gid_list is used for MDS cap checks only. Kernel message v3 (legacy head) loses gid_list, v4 loses alternate_name and fscrypt fields.

features.name: Request data segment uses
features.description: Initial xattrs (ACLs/security labels) for new inodes, setxattr values, fscrypt last block on truncate, SnapPayload for mksnap, key/value/op for snap metadata.
features.notes: Kernel sends POSIX ACLs at create time (linux/fs/ceph/acl.c:200).

features.name: Op code dispatch table (CEPH_MDS_OP_*)
features.description: 32 client-visible op codes mapped to Server handlers; unknown or internal (0x15xx) ops get -EOPNOTSUPP; W bit drives may_write (EROFS, completed-request recording).
features.notes: READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF carry the W bit although read-like.

features.name: Read-only cache and full-pool request gating
features.description: may_write ops get -EROFS on a read-only cache; with the metadata pool FULL, SETLAYOUT/SETDIRLAYOUT/RMXATTR/SETXATTR/CREATE/SYMLINK/MKSNAP and LINK/RENAME before peer requests get -ENOSPC unless the caller has the full MDS cap.

features.name: MClientReply head and errno conventions
features.description: 15-byte ceph_mds_reply_head (op, result as Linux errno via errorcode32_t, mdsmap_epoch, safe, is_dentry, is_target) followed by trace_bl, extra_bl, snapbl bufferlists.
features.notes: mdsmap_epoch is 0 in early replies.

features.name: Reply trace (dir InodeStat, DirStat, dname, LeaseStat, target InodeStat) and snap trace
features.description: set_trace_dist builds the dentry and target trace; DirStat carries frag, auth and replica dist used by clients for MDS selection; snapbl holds the realm snap trace for head requests.

features.name: InodeStat encoding v9 (REPLY_ENCODING) and legacy feature-conditional encoding
features.description: ENCODE_START(9,1) InodeStat with caps, layout, times, sizes, dirstat/rstat, fragtree, symlink, dir_layout, xattrs, inline data, quota, pool_ns, btime, change_attr, dir_pin(v2), snap_btime(v3), rsnaps(v4), snap_metadata(v5), fscrypt flag(v6), fscrypt_auth/file(v7), optmetadata charmap/quarantine(v8), subvolume_id(v9); legacy form gated by connection features.
features.notes: Fixed prefix equals kernel struct ceph_mds_reply_inode (221 bytes).

features.name: Cap issuance and xattr/inline inclusion inside InodeStat
features.description: Encoding an inode for a client adds a Capability if missing and issues (wanted|likes)&allowed; xattrs/inline data are included based on client cap versions and getattr mask.
features.notes: Wire-visible side effect of every reply; owned by capabilities.md.

features.name: Dentry lease issuance in replies (LeaseStat)
features.description: LeaseStat v2 (mask, duration_ms 30000, seq, alternate_name) or null lease when not grantable.

features.name: Snap trace old/new format selection
features.description: SnapRealmInfo (raw head + snap lists) or SnapRealmInfoNew (versioned with last_modified, change_attr, flags) chained from realm to root, selected by NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO.
features.notes: Kernel 7.3 does not advertise NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO.

features.name: Readdir / lssnap / readdir_snapdiff extra_bl listing format
features.description: DirStat, u32 count, u16 flags (FRAG_END, FRAG_COMPLETE, HASH_ORDER, OFFSET_HASH), entries of name + LeaseStat + InodeStat; resume via path2 name or offset_hash; byte/entry budgets.

features.name: Create reply with created ino and delegated inode ranges
features.description: CREATE replies carry openc_response_t (created_ino + delegated_inos interval set) when the Server::mds_allow_async_dirops member is true and the client has DELEG_INO, else raw u64 ino with REPLY_CREATE_INODE. Clients pick the parser from the MDS's DELEG_INO bit, not from the reply.
features.notes: Kernel caps delegated inos at 8192 per session and ignores ranges below 0x1000. With mds_allow_async_dirops turned off at runtime the raw u64 form breaks both clients (kernel -EIO; libcephfs unguarded decode) - derived from code.

features.name: GETFILELOCK, GETVXATTR and FILE_BLOCKDIFF extra_bl payloads
features.description: Raw ceph_filelock; ENCODE_START(1,1){string value}; BlockDiff ENCODE_START(1,1){rval, scan_idx, interval_set blocks}.
features.notes: Kernel getvxattr parser requires exact length.

features.name: Early (unsafe) reply and safe reply
features.description: Mutations get an unsafe reply with trace before journal commit (unless replay, journaled peers, InoTable allocation, MDS requester, mds_early_reply=false) and a safe reply without trace after commit.
features.notes: Clients replay requests that only got an unsafe reply after MDS failure.

features.name: Request forwarding via MClientRequestForward
features.description: A non-auth rank never relays; it tells the client dest_mds and num_fwd+1 (client_must_resend always true); client resends to dest; num_fwd must strictly increase or the client aborts with EMULTIHOP.
code_refs: src/mds/MDCache.cc:8821 (path_traverse discovers instead of forwarding when depth < num_fwd)
features.notes: Kernel reads only dest_mds and num_fwd. The MDS reads ext_num_fwd in path_traverse to bound ping-pong.

features.name: Retry/replay idempotency via session completed_requests
features.description: Successful may_write requests (except SETFILELOCK) are recorded per session with the created ino; replayed or retried tids are answered traceless (plus created ino) or converted to LOOKUP/GETATTR, CREATE/OPEN re-executed as open; trimmed by oldest_client_tid.
features.notes: Durable session state; see sessions.md and journal pages.

features.name: Replay handling during up:reconnect
features.description: REPLAY/ASYNC requests arriving before the rank is active are queued for clientreplay and their head.ino reserved; completed retried requests are queued too.
features.notes: Kernel replays unsafe requests before sending MClientReconnect.

features.name: Client-chosen inode numbers (head.ino) for async create and replay
features.description: prepare_new_inode honours head.ino from the session prealloc/delegated set or the InoTable, otherwise allocates another and logs a cluster error.
features.notes: Kernel async create depends on the MDS using exactly the delegated ino.

features.name: Getattr/lookup batching
features.description: Concurrent identical getattr/lookup requests are batched; all members get the same trace or are all forwarded.
features.notes: mds_allow_batched_ops.

features.name: MClientCaps encoding v14 (xattrs in middle segment)
features.description: Raw caps head + non-export body or padded export peer, snap trace, xattr middle, then versioned tail up to v14 (flock, peer, inline, osd barrier, oldest flush tid, caller uid/gid, pool_ns, btime/change_attr, flags, dirstat, fscrypt, subvolume_id, oserrno).
features.notes: Kernel sends v12 and parses up to v12.

features.name: MClientCapRelease with OSD epoch barrier
features.description: Batched (ino, cap_id, migrate_seq, issue_seq) records plus osd_epoch_barrier that pauses MDS RADOS ops until that epoch.

features.name: MClientLease protocol (revoke, release, renew, revoke_ack)
features.description: 35-byte raw lease head + dname; MDS revokes, renews and removes leases by seq.
features.notes: Any other action from a client on a dentry it holds a lease on reaches ceph_abort() (Locker.cc:4535). Kernel uses userspace CEPH_LOCK_DN=1 vs its own =2; mask is ignored on revoke.

features.name: MClientSnap realm update/split notifications
features.description: Raw snap head + split inos + split realms + snap trace. Per-realm notifications (do_realm_invalidate_and_update_notify, prepare_realm_split/merge) are always op SPLIT, with split lists only for a real split; global-snaprealm notifications after a snap-table commit are UPDATE (DESTROY for rmsnap) to every open/stale session; reconnect catch-up is UPDATE. CREATE is never sent to clients.
features.notes: mksnap's CREATE, rmsnap's DESTROY and renamesnap's UPDATE reach clients as SPLIT with empty split lists.

features.name: MClientQuota rstat/quota push
features.description: ino, rctime, rbytes, rfiles, rsubdirs, quota_info_t pushed to cap holders of quota realm inodes on significant change.
features.notes: Clients enforce quotas; MDS never returns EDQUOT.

features.name: MClientReconnect encodings v1..v5 (data segment, multi-message)
features.description: Map of ino -> cap_reconnect_t (path, cap record, flock blob, snap_follows) and snaprealm records; v5 'more' flag for multi-message reconnect.
features.notes: Kernel sends v3 (v2 without MDSENC) and v5 only when splitting past RECONNECT_MAX_SIZE; never v4. The per-cap lock blob is decoded later without try (Server::recover_filelocks).

features.name: Session reclaim (MClientReclaim/MClientReclaimReply)
features.description: A new session can reclaim (kill/evict) an older session with the same uuid metadata and same cephx entity, returning the OSDMap epoch to wait for and the old address.
features.notes: Kernel does not implement reclaim (bit 10 not advertised).

features.name: Client metrics upload (MClientMetrics) incl. subvolume metrics
features.description: Vector of typed ENCODE_START payloads (cap info, latencies, leases, opened files/inodes, io sizes, subvolume metrics) handled by MetricsHandler outside mds_lock.
features.notes: Kernel 7.3 gates subvolume metrics on feature bit 22.

features.name: Quarantine notifications and gating
features.description: MQuarantineDisable(ino, oserrno=0) to quarantine-aware sessions when quarantine is lifted; non-aware clients are blocked on quarantined subtrees; quarantine optmetadata in InodeStat v8.
features.notes: Kernel 7.3 does not advertise bit 24. InodeStat's QUARANTINE optmetadata is always a default-constructed record (enabled=true, timestamp 0), not the stored one (CInode.cc:4133-4137).

features.name: Charmap (case-insensitive directories) gating
features.description: openc/mkdir/symlink/link/rename (not mknod) into charmap directories return EPERM for clients lacking CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP; charmap optmetadata carried in InodeStat v8.
features.notes: Kernel 7.3 sets bit 22 with a different meaning (SUBVOLUME_METRICS).

features.name: Counted messages and session push_seq
features.description: Caps, lease, snap, quota and quarantine-disable messages increment Session push_seq; client counts the same messages and must echo the count in REQUEST_CLOSE; FLUSHMSG uses it as a barrier.
features.notes: Kernel counter: linux/fs/ceph/super.c:1524 (ceph_inc_mds_stopping_blocker).

features.name: MDS-originated MClientRequest (internal)
features.description: Ranks send MClientRequest to peers for stray reintegration/migration renames and quota realm creation, and accept MClientReply for them.
features.notes: Not part of the client contract.

features.name: CephFS feature names for mon commands and dumps
features.description: feature_names table maps bits to names (reserved, jewel ... quarantine) used by 'fs required_client_features' and session dumps.
features.notes: cephfs_feature_name() checks id > size, so id 25 indexes one past the array (cephfs_features.cc:45).

features.name: Client-triggerable aborts in decode and handlers
features.description: ceph_assert in decode_payload (MClientCaps xattr_len vs middle; MClientReply/MClientSnap/MClientQuota trailing bytes), ceph_assert(is_safe) on a client-sent MClientReply, ceph_abort on an unexpected MClientLease action, and unguarded buffer decodes of client blobs (initial xattrs, fscrypt last-block header, reconnect lock blob) abort the MDS.
features.notes: Derived from code; unmodified clients do not send such input.

features.name: dmClock QoS queue between dispatch and request handling
features.description: With mds_dmclock_enable (default false) and valid volume info on an active rank, client requests are queued per volume (session metadata root) and executed later by the scheduler thread under mds_lock; other client messages bypass the queue.
features.notes: Breaks request-vs-cap-message FIFO for a connection when enabled (derived from code). Owned by qos-dmclock-scheduler.md.

serialization_points.name: Single DispatchQueue thread for all client messages
serialization_points.why_serialized: The MDS registers no fast-dispatch handlers; every client message is delivered by one dispatch thread to MDSDaemon::ms_dispatch2.
serialization_points.notes: Decoding is parallel in worker threads; only delivery is serialized.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around all client message handling
serialization_points.shared_state: entire MDS cache, sessions, locks, journal submission
serialization_points.why_serialized: Coarse global lock protects all MDS state.
serialization_points.notes: True conflicts are per session (session/caps msgs) and per inode/dentry (requests).

serialization_points.name: Laggy-beacon deferral queue
serialization_points.why_serialized: When the beacon is laggy every message is deferred and later replayed in order.

serialization_points.name: Reply trace construction under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: CInode projected/committed inode, caps, leases, snaprealm cache
serialization_points.why_serialized: encode_inodestat reads inode views and mutates Capability/lease state while building the reply.
serialization_points.notes: Cap issuance in the reply must be atomic with respect to the inode's lock state; byte encoding itself could be parallel.

serialization_points.name: Session push_seq counter
serialization_points.why_serialized: Counted message order must match the client's count for REQUEST_CLOSE and FLUSHMSG.
serialization_points.notes: Counter plus send order on the session connection must be consistent.

serialization_points.name: Session completed_requests table
serialization_points.why_serialized: Idempotency record must be updated when the reply is sent and trimmed by oldest_client_tid.
serialization_points.notes: Per-session map; entries for different tids commute.

serialization_points.name: Active request registry
serialization_points.notes: Global map in C++, but conflicts only exist per (client, tid).

serialization_points.name: Clientreplay one-at-a-time queue
serialization_points.why_serialized: Replayed requests are dispatched one at a time in arrival order.
serialization_points.notes: Ordering among requests of one client and touching the same objects is what matters.

serialization_points.name: Per-connection message ordering
serialization_points.why_serialized: Clients rely on in-order delivery of replies, caps, leases and snaps of one session, and the MDS on in-order client requests/releases/cap flushes.

serialization_points.name: Session open journaling before OPEN reply
serialization_points.why_serialized: OPEN is only sent after ESession is safe.

serialization_points.name: dmClock scheduler thread
serialization_points.shared_state: per-volume dmClock queues, then everything under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Optional QoS: requests are dequeued by one thread that takes mds_lock for each request.
serialization_points.notes: Default off. Requests can be overtaken by later cap/lease messages of the same session.

serialization_points.name: Forward depth vs discover
serialization_points.shared_state: request ext_num_fwd, replica state of the path
serialization_points.why_serialized: After num_fwd forwards the rank replicates (discovers) the remaining path instead of forwarding again.

external_contract.detail: CLIENT_SESSION 22, RECONNECT 23, REQUEST 24, REQUEST_FORWARD 25, REPLY 26, METRICS 29, CAPS 0x310, LEASE 0x311, SNAP 0x312, CAPRELEASE 0x313, QUOTA 0x314; kernel does not know 27/28/0x315.
Same as kernel plus RECLAIM 27, RECLAIM_REPLY 28, QUARANTINE_DISABLE 0x315.
msgr v1 protocol version 32 for MDS connections.
MClientSession v>=3 with feature_bitset_t (kernel reads first u64 word, overwritten on every OPEN), v5 flags, v6 cap_auths parsed positionally (MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch v1 layout frozen).
supported_features and metric_spec stored and overwritten on every OPEN, duplicates included (the C++ duplicate-OPEN reply has no metric_spec); cap_auths stored for local checks.
MDS sends OPEN, CLOSE, RENEWCAPS, STALE, RECALL_STATE(max_caps), FLUSHMSG(seq), FORCE_RO, REJECT; libcephfs aborts on any other op.
Kernel sends hostname, kernel_version, entity_id, root; MDS validates root against caps and uses it for QoS volume id.
hostname, pid, entity_id, root, ceph_version, ceph_sha1, client_metadata pairs, uuid, timeout.
Ganesha sets uuid metadata and uses MClientReclaim (RESET, FINISH) to take over the old instance's session; reply carries OSDMap epoch and old address.
REJECT with SESSION_BLOCKLISTED flag (v5+) or, in v3/v4 messages only, error_string containing 'blacklisted'.
Message v3 legacy head, v4 head v1, v6 head v2/v3 (struct_len 118, owner_uid/gid for new-inode ops); full tail (stamp, gids, altname, fscrypt) always sent.
Message v6; head v1/v2/v3 by MDS bits 18/20; legacy head without FS_BTIME.
REPLAY on resend after unsafe reply (head.ino = target ino), WANT_DENTRY when a parent is set, ASYNC for async create/unlink.
Initial xattrs (POSIX ACLs, security labels) for create/mknod/mkdir/symlink as u32 count + (string, u32 len+bytes).

LOOKUP, GETATTR, LOOKUPPARENT, LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPNAME, GETVXATTR, SETXATTR, RMXATTR, SETLAYOUT, SETATTR, SETFILELOCK, GETFILELOCK, SETDIRLAYOUT, MKNOD, LINK, UNLINK, RENAME, MKDIR, RMDIR, SYMLINK, CREATE, OPEN, READDIR, LOOKUPSNAP, MKSNAP, RMSNAP, LSSNAP, RENAMESNAP.
Kernel set minus SETLAYOUT/SETDIRLAYOUT plus LOOKUPHASH, READDIR_SNAPDIFF, FILE_BLOCKDIFF, SNAP_METADATA.

With REPLY_ENCODING: struct_compat must be 1 for InodeStat/DirStat/LeaseStat/quota; trace consumed exactly; extra_bl only for GETFILELOCK/READDIR/LSSNAP/CREATE/GETVXATTR; whole front consumed; getvxattr payload exact.
ino..fragtree nsplits identical to packed struct ceph_mds_reply_inode (221 bytes); InodeStat v9 adds subvolume_id read by the kernel.
At most one unsafe then one safe reply per tid; safe content ignored after unsafe; unsafe requests are replayed after MDS restart.
MClientRequestForward {i32 dest_mds, i32 num_fwd, bool must_resend}; num_fwd must increase strictly else EMULTIHOP.
auth (-1 = same as dir inode auth) and replica dist used by __choose_mds for subsequent requests.
openc_response_t delegated ranges, each >= 0x1000, total per session <= 8192; kernel creates async files with those inos.
Caps/lease/snap/quota counted on both sides; REQUEST_CLOSE seq must equal MDS push_seq.
Negative Linux errno in reply head result.
Kernel 7.3 uses bit 22 for SUBVOLUME_METRICS; Ceph uses bit 22 for CHARMAP.
Kernel consults FS_BTIME (bit 59), MDSENC, SERVER_LUMINOUS on the MDS connection; REPLY_CREATE_INODE/MDS_INLINE_DATA/MDS_QUOTA/FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 only without CephFS bit 9.
MDS sends v14 (kernel parses to v12, ignores v13/v14); kernel sends v12; 92-byte head + 84-byte body; xattrs in middle segment; flush tid in header tid.
Kernel sends v3 (v2 without MDSENC) or v5 multi-message with MULTI_RECONNECT past RECONNECT_MAX_SIZE; payload in data segment; replays unsafe requests and resends already-sent requests first.
Sent only to MDS with METRIC_COLLECT; subvolume metrics (type 16, u64 count of AggregatedIOMetrics) only when MDS advertises bit 22.
Subvolume metrics gated on MDS metric_spec bit 16.
MQuarantineDisable(ino, oserrno) for QUARANTINE-capable sessions; quarantine optmetadata in InodeStat v8.
MDSMap per-fs required CephFS feature bitmap edited by 'fs required_client_features'; MDS rejects/evicts sessions lacking bits.
MClientCapRelease v2 osd_epoch_barrier makes the MDS Objecter wait for that OSDMap epoch.
Request stamp (client time) becomes ctime/mtime/btime of mutations.
Async dirops rely on DELEG_INO, delegated inos in create replies and dir caps Fc/Fr (CEPH_CAP_DIR_CREATE/UNLINK).
libcephfs counts caps, lease, snap and quota messages (Client::got_mds_push) but not MQuarantineDisable, which the C++ MDS sends counted; REQUEST_CLOSE seq must equal MDS push_seq.
A READDIR/LSSNAP reply must not carry more entries than args.readdir.max_entries; the kernel sizes its preallocated entry buffer from it and fails an overflowing reply with -EIO.
If the MDS advertised DELEG_INO, every non-empty CREATE extra_bl is parsed as openc_response_t (kernel skips 6 header bytes); a raw u64 then fails with -EIO. libcephfs makes the same choice.
Clients receive SPLIT for per-realm updates (split lists may be empty) and UPDATE/DESTROY for the global snaprealm; never CREATE.

rust_implications.implication: All client-facing structures (request head v1-v3 with struct_len skip, InodeStat v9, DirStat, LeaseStat v2, snap traces, extra_bl formats, MClientCaps v14, MClientSession v7, reconnect v1-v5, metrics) must be reproduced byte-for-byte; generate golden vectors from the C++ encoders (ceph-dencoder / unit tests) and from kernel parsers before writing handlers.

Keep struct_compat = 1 for every versioned sub-encoding sent to clients, only append fields, never put extra_bl on ops other than GETFILELOCK/READDIR/LSSNAP/CREATE/GETVXATTR (fix the C++ retried-mkdir extra_bl behaviour), keep getvxattr payload exact, and keep MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch v1 layout since the kernel ignores struct_len.

Decide explicitly what the Rust MDS advertises at CephFS bit 22: advertising it tells kernel 7.3 to send subvolume metrics (useful for per-subvolume SLA telemetry) but tells libcephfs/C++ semantics 'charmap'; not advertising it makes kernel 7.3 skip subvolume metrics. Gate charmap behaviour on something other than bit 22 for kernel sessions, or not support charmap.

Advertise at least bits 0-9, 11-18, 20, 21 (and 10, 19, 23, 24 if implemented); keep all used bits below 64 because the kernel only reads the first word. Connection-level features must include FS_BTIME, MDSENC, SERVER_LUMINOUS, EXPORT_PEER, FLOCK, REPLY_CREATE_INODE, MDS_INLINE_DATA, MDS_QUOTA, FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2.

Decode, route and execute client messages on a worker pool keyed by shard (subvolume/dirfrag/inode) instead of one dispatch thread + mds_lock, but preserve per-session ordering where the protocol needs it: requests vs piggy-backed releases, cap flushes vs subsequent requests, and the MDS's send order of replies/caps/leases/snaps on the session connection.

push_seq (counted messages), completed_requests, completed_flushes, prealloc/delegated inos are per-session state touched by many shards; model the session as its own actor/shard with an atomic send sequencer so counted messages are numbered in the exact order they are written to the connection.

Encoding an InodeStat issues caps and leases as a side effect; in a sharded design the reply encoder must run inside the inode's shard (or take the inode lock) so cap state and the encoded snapshot are consistent; the byte encoding itself can then happen outside locks.

Unsafe reply after journal submission and safe reply after commit maps naturally to per-shard journals; cross-shard (2PC) operations must suppress early replies like the C++ 'journaled peers' rule, or prove that exposing uncommitted state is safe for clients that replay.

completed_requests must be durable and reachable from whichever shard re-executes a retried/replayed tid (store it in a per-session journal or replicate into the owning shard's journal with the op), and trimmed by oldest_client_tid from requests and RENEWCAPS v7.
Internal shards inside one rank never need MClientRequestForward; forwarding is only required when the authoritative rank differs. num_fwd must still increase strictly per forward.
head.ino from delegated ranges must be honoured exactly (kernel creates the inode locally); delegation per session must stay <= 8192 and >= 0x1000.

Validate peer type for CLIENT_REPLY (C++ asserts), never assert on owner_uid=-1, zero cap_id/wanted for snapped inodes, set mdsmap_epoch in early replies if harmless, avoid ceph_abort-inducing session ops toward libcephfs.
Session metadata 'root' (and auth caps path) is the natural key for per-subvolume QoS/rate limits; the C++ dmClock scheduler already uses it.
READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF carry the W bit; the Rust MDS can treat them as reads (no completed-request record, no EROFS) without breaking clients.
Return only negative Linux errno values that clients already handle (list in the page); EDQUOT is client-side; MClientReclaimReply.result is a raw i32.

Only count message types that every client counts (caps, lease, snap, quota); send MQuarantineDisable (or any new MDS->client message) uncounted unless all supported clients count it, otherwise session close handshakes break.

rust_implications.topic: Choose encodings from feature bits only
rust_implications.implication: Pick the CREATE extra_bl format (openc_response_t vs raw u64) from the negotiated DELEG_INO bit, not from a runtime option, because clients choose the parser from the MDS's advertised bit; likewise send the same supported_features and metric_spec in every OPEN, duplicates included.

Validate segment lengths, trailing bytes, lease actions and embedded blobs (initial xattrs, fscrypt headers, reconnect lock blobs) and answer with an error or drop the message, instead of reproducing the C++ asserts.
Treat args.readdir.max_entries and max_bytes as hard limits for READDIR, LSSNAP and READDIR_SNAPDIFF; the kernel buffer is sized from them.

open_questions: Kernel 7.3.0-rc6 numbers CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS as 22 while Ceph main uses 22 for CHARMAP: which numbering will upstream Linux and Ceph converge on, and what should the Rust MDS advertise?

Is the C++ behaviour of returning a created-ino extra_bl to a retried MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK (kernel -EIO) reachable in practice? It needs a non-REPLAY resend with num_retry > 0 of a completed tid reaching a rank that is not in clientreplay (resends during up:reconnect are converted to LOOKUP/GETATTR instead). Verify with a test.
Should the Rust MDS keep supporting legacy (pre-REPLY_ENCODING / pre-FS_BTIME) encodings at all, given only very old kernels need them?

libcephfs does not count MQuarantineDisable while the MDS sends it counted; confirm by test that a later REQUEST_CLOSE from libcephfs is dropped (Server.cc:860) and decide whether the Rust MDS should send it uncounted.
Does turning mds_allow_async_dirops off at runtime really break kernel CREATE replies with -EIO and crash libcephfs (derived from code)? Verify with a test.
With mds_dmclock_enable, can a client's cap/lease message overtaking its queued request (e.g. an async create followed by cap updates on the new inode) cause visible misbehaviour?
Does libcephfs ever send a duplicate REQUEST_OPEN to an open session in practice, and does losing the metric spec afterwards matter?
